The temperature is further increased from $T_2$ to $T_3$ such that the increase in its length is $\Delta L_2$. Given $T_3+T_1=2T_2$ and $T_2-T_1=\Delta T$, the value of $\Delta L_2$ is ______.
questions.question: The temperature of a metal strip having coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha$ is increased from $T_1$ to $T_2$ resulting in increase of its length by $\Delta L_1$. The temperature is further increased from $T_2$ to $T_3$ such that the increase in its length is $\Delta L_2$. Given $T_3+T_1=2T_2$ and $T_2-T_1=\Delta T$, the value of $\Delta L_2$ is ______.
questions.solution:
Let the length of the metal strip at temperature $T_1$ be $L_1$.

When the temperature is increased from $T_1$ to $T_2$, the new length $L_2$ is given by:

$L_2 = L_1(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$

where $\Delta T = T_2 - T_1$.

The increase in length is:

$\Delta L_1 = L_2 - L_1 = L_1 \alpha \Delta T$

When the temperature is further increased from $T_2$ to $T_3$, the new length $L_3$ is:

$L_3 = L_2(1 + \alpha \Delta T')$

where $\Delta T' = T_3 - T_2$.

Given $T_3 + T_1 = 2T_2$, we have $T_3 - T_2 = T_2 - T_1 = \Delta T$.

Thus, $\Delta T' = \Delta T$.

The increase in length for this second temperature change is:

$\Delta L_2 = L_3 - L_2 = L_2 \alpha \Delta T$

Substituting $L_2 = L_1(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$ into the equation for $\Delta L_2$:

$\Delta L_2 = L_1(1 + \alpha \Delta T) \alpha \Delta T$

$\Delta L_2 = (L_1 \alpha \Delta T)(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$

Since $\Delta L_1 = L_1 \alpha \Delta T$, substituting this gives:

$\Delta L_2 = \Delta L_1(1 + \alpha \Delta T)$

Answer: $\Delta L_1[1+\alpha\Delta T]$

questions.q: An ideal gas at pressure $P$ and temperature $T$ is expanding such that $PT^3 = $ constant. The coefficient of volume expansion of the gas is _______.
questions.question: An ideal gas at pressure $P$ and temperature $T$ is expanding such that $PT^3 = $ constant. The coefficient of volume expansion of the gas is _______.
questions.solution:
Given the process equation for the ideal gas:

$PT^3 = \text{constant}$

From the ideal gas equation, $PV = nRT$, which gives $P = \dfrac{nRT}{V}$.

Substituting $P$ into the process equation:

$\left(\dfrac{nRT}{V}\right) T^3 = \text{constant}$

$\dfrac{T^4}{V} = \text{constant}$

$V = k T^4$

Differentiating both sides with respect to temperature $T$:

$\dfrac{dV}{dT} = 4k T^3$

The coefficient of volume expansion $\gamma$ is defined as:

$\gamma = \dfrac{1}{V} \dfrac{dV}{dT}$

Substituting the values of $V$ and $\dfrac{dV}{dT}$:

$\gamma = \dfrac{1}{k T^4} (4k T^3) = \dfrac{4}{T}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4}{T}$

questions.question: A block of ice at $- 10 ° C$ is slowly heated and converted to steam at $100 ° C$. Which of the following curves represent the phenomenon qualitatively:

When the state of the substance is not changing, temperature of the substance increases when heat is supplied to it. But when the substance changes the state, the heat supplied to it used as latent heat and the temperature remains constant until all the substance converts to other state.

questions.solution:
Heat extracted to cool $x$ gram of water from $50^{\circ}\text{C}$ to $0^{\circ}\text{C}$ is given by:

$Q_1 = m_1 c \Delta T_1$

$Q_2 = m_2 c \Delta T_2 + m_2 L$

$Q_2 = (1000 - x) \times [4.2 \times (100 - 50) + 2256]$

$Q_1 = Q_2$

$210x = 2466(1000 - x)$

$210x = 2466000 - 2466x$

$2676x = 2466000$

$x = \dfrac{2466000}{2676} \approx 921.52$

The closest integer value for $x$ is $922$.

Answer: $922$

questions.question: A body cools from $60 ° C$ to $40 ° C$ in $6$ minutes. If, temperature of surroundings is $10 ° C$. Then, after the next $6$ minutes, its temperature will be ______ $° C$.
questions.solution:
From Newton’s law of cooling

$\dfrac{d T}{d t} = k\left({T}_{avg} - {T}_{0}\right)$, here, ${T}_{0}$ is surrounding temperature.

For case $1$:

$\dfrac{60 - 40}{6} = k\left(\dfrac{60 + 40}{2} - 10\right)$

$\dfrac{20}{6} = k\left(50 - 10\right) . . . \left(1\right)$

For case $2$:

$\dfrac{40 - T}{6} = k\left(\dfrac{40 + T}{2} - 10\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation $\left(1\right)$, we have $k = \dfrac{1}{12}$

Putting in equation $\left(2\right)$

$\dfrac{40 - T}{6} = \dfrac{1}{12}\left(\dfrac{40 + T}{2} - 10\right)$

$⇒ 10 + \dfrac{T}{2} = 80 - 2T ⇒ 2T + \dfrac{T}{2} = 70$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{140}{5} = 28 ° C$

questions.solution:
From Newton's law of cooling, we have

$\dfrac{\DeltaQ}{\Deltat} = - K\left({T}_{avg} - {T}_{0}\right)$

Where, $Q = ms ∆ T$, $m$ is the mass, $s$ is the specific heat and $∆ T$ is the temperature change.

Case $1:$

$∆ t = 2minutes, {T}_{0} = 22 ° C$

$\dfrac{ms \times 12}{2} = - K\left(\dfrac{98 + 86}{2} - 22\right)$

$6 = - \dfrac{K}{ms}\left(70\right) . . . \left(1\right)$

Case $2:$

$\dfrac{ms \times 6}{\Deltat} = - K\left(\dfrac{75 + 69}{2} - 22\right)$

$\dfrac{6}{\Deltat} = - \dfrac{K}{ms} ( 50 ) . . . \left(2\right)$

Dividing (2) by (1), we get

$⇒ \dfrac{6}{\Deltat ( 6 )} = \dfrac{50}{70}$

$⇒ \Deltat = \dfrac{7}{5} = 1 . 4min$
